nodes.skill_target: connect announced sign to named Judas in John
nodes.player_prompt: Який знак називає Ісус у відповідь на питання «хто це?» і кому дає шматок?
nodes.accepted_answer: The betrayer is the one to whom Jesus will give the dipped morsel/piece; he gives it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon.
nodes.rejected_answers: John leaves the recipient unnamed here.
nodes.success_feedback: Johannine sign linked correctly to Judas in John 13:26; recipient identity is explicit in this witness.
nodes.partial_feedback: Keep the dipped-morsel sign but add the explicit recipient or citation; do not make John leave him unnamed.
nodes.failure_feedback: Read John 13:26: identify both the announced sign and the person who receives it.

hints.H4: Then identify who receives the dipped morsel.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: the betrayer is the one to receive the dipped morsel; Jesus gives it to Judas Iscariot, son of Simon. John 13:26 directly supports both parts. Mastery=guided.

nodes.on_hint_threshold: Deliver H7 answer+evidence; set mastery_mode=guided; then LN03-N10
nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Plain text answer with explicit source label; no image of the table required.

nodes.why_this_node_exists: teaches local order without universalizing it
nodes.player_prompt: Розташуйте за Ів 13:26–30: give morsel → Satan enters → command → misunderstanding → Judas leaves.
nodes.accepted_answer: Give morsel to Judas → Satan enters him → Jesus says do it quickly → others misunderstand → Judas goes out.
nodes.rejected_answers: Importing Synoptic steps into this local ordering task.
nodes.rejection_reason: The task is scoped to John's local sequence.
nodes.success_feedback: John-local sequence reconstructed without importing Synoptic steps or treating it as universal chronology.
nodes.partial_feedback: Keep correctly ordered John steps and move only the misplaced item; no cross-witness insertion.
nodes.failure_feedback: Read John 13:26–30 as a local chain: morsel, entry, command, misunderstanding, exit.

hints.H1: Goal: local chronology in John only.
hints.H2: Start with the morsel in v.26.
hints.H3: Then note what follows in v.27.
hints.H4: Separate Jesus' command from the diners' misunderstanding.
hints.H5: The exit is last in this scoped chain.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: give morsel → Satan enters → Jesus says act quickly → others misunderstand → Judas leaves. This is John-local order, not a four-Gospel master timeline. Mastery=guided.

nodes.on_hint_threshold: Deliver H7 answer+evidence; set mastery_mode=guided; then LN03-N11
nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Numeric positions and move-up/move-down controls; drag-and-drop is never required.

nodes.why_this_node_exists: distinguishes reader knowledge from what diners understood
nodes.player_prompt: Чи зрозуміли інші за столом причину слів Ісуса Юді? Які два пояснення вони припускали?
nodes.accepted_answer: No. Some thought Judas should buy what was needed for the feast or give something to the poor because he had the money box.
nodes.accepted_variants: The two explanations may be given in any order.
nodes.rejected_answers: Everyone understood Judas was leaving to betray Jesus.
nodes.success_feedback: Character-knowledge boundary preserved: the diners do not understand the true reason and infer purchase-for-feast or giving-to-poor.
nodes.partial_feedback: If you gave only one mistaken explanation, add the other; if you said they knew the betrayal plan, remove that overclaim.
nodes.failure_feedback: Read John 13:28–29 and list the two explanations actually reported by the narrator.

hints.H1: Goal: what the diners understood, not what the reader knows.
hints.H4: The other concerns giving to the poor.
hints.H5: The money box explains why these guesses were plausible.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: No; they thought Judas might buy what was needed for the feast or give something to the poor because he kept the money box. Mastery=guided.

nodes.on_hint_threshold: Deliver H7 answer+evidence; set mastery_mode=guided; then LN03-N12
nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Two labelled text slots plus yes/no state; all feedback announced textually.

nodes.player_prompt: Класифікуйте п'ять ключових тверджень місії як T1/T2/unsupported.
nodes.accepted_answer: Matthew names Judas=T1; Luke names Judas in 22:21–23=unsupported; all four announce betrayal by one present=T2; John says others understood true reason=unsupported; Mark says one of the Twelve=T1.
nodes.success_feedback: All five claims now preserve the distinction between direct text, cross-witness comparison and unsupported import.
nodes.partial_feedback: Retry only the misclassified claim; do not erase correct classifications.
nodes.failure_feedback: For each statement ask: is it in this witness directly, only from comparison, or absent from the cited text?

hints.H4: The four-witness betrayal announcement is comparative T2.
hints.H5: John reports misunderstanding, not correct understanding.
hints.H6: Mark explicitly says one of the Twelve.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: Matthew names Judas=T1; Luke naming Judas=unsupported; common betrayal announcement=T2; John others understood=true is unsupported; Mark one of Twelve=T1. Mastery=guided.

nodes.on_hint_threshold: Deliver H7 answer+evidence; set mastery_mode=guided; then LN03-N13
nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Each statement is a separate labelled classification group with source/confidence announced.

nodes.skill_target: produce four-witness reconstruction with chronology limit
nodes.player_prompt: Складіть реконструкцію: common core; Matthew; Luke; John; заверште chronology-limit statement.
nodes.accepted_answer: Must include common betrayal announcement; Matthew Judas question; Luke hand-at-table and mutual inquiry without naming Judas; John's Peter→beloved disciple inquiry, dipped morsel to Judas, subsequent local sequence and others' misunderstanding; exact cross-witness minute-by-minute order not forced.
nodes.accepted_variants: Any source-grounded equivalent with citations from all four witnesses.
nodes.required_evidence: Citations from all four primary passages.
nodes.rejected_answers: Flattened narrative erasing witness differences or claiming exact global order.
nodes.success_feedback: Mission synthesis preserves common core, each witness's distinctive evidence, John's local order and an explicit uncertainty boundary.
nodes.partial_feedback: Keep correct witness blocks; repair only the missing provenance, citation or chronology-limit statement.
nodes.failure_feedback: Rebuild under four headings: common core / Matthew / Luke / John, then add one sentence that exact cross-witness minute-by-minute order is not established.

hints.H2: Common core: betrayal by one present.
hints.H3: Matthew: Judas question; Luke: hand-at-table and inquiry.
hints.H4: John: Peter→beloved disciple, morsel to Judas, local sequence, misunderstanding.
hints.H5: Do not make Luke explicitly name Judas.
hints.H6: Use citations from all four assigned passages.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: state the common betrayal announcement; Matthew's Judas question; Luke's hand-at-table and mutual inquiry without naming Judas; John's inquiry chain, morsel to Judas, local sequence and others' misunderstanding; finish that exact global chronology is not forced. Mastery=guided; then mission complete.

nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Four ordered headings with multiline text and citation fields; no visual board required.

nodes.why_this_node_exists: adds intertextual evidence while keeping broader typology separate
nodes.player_prompt: Знайдіть старозавітний текст, на який вказує Ів 13:18, і назвіть лише текстовий зв'язок.
nodes.accepted_answer: Psalm 41:9 (verse numbering may vary); motif of a close bread-sharing companion turning against the speaker.
nodes.accepted_variants: Verse-numbering variants accepted; broader typology not required.
nodes.rejected_answers: Treating a broad theological theory as direct T1 from the cross-reference.
nodes.rejection_reason: The task establishes textual relation only.
nodes.success_feedback: Cross-testament relation is limited to the textual bread-sharing companion motif; broader theology is not graded as direct text.
nodes.partial_feedback: Keep the Psalm reference and textual motif; remove unproved typological expansion.
nodes.failure_feedback: Read John 13:18 together with Psalm 41:9 and state only the explicit textual relation.

hints.H2: Old Testament target: Psalm 41:9; numbering may vary.
hints.H3: Look for a bread-sharing companion motif.
hints.H4: Do not convert the relation into a full theology.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: Psalm 41:9; shared motif is a close bread-sharing companion turning against the speaker. Broader typology is not required. Mastery=guided.

nodes.on_hint_threshold: Deliver H7 answer+evidence; set mastery_mode=guided; then MISSION_COMPLETE
nodes.functional_nonvisual_equivalent: Two linear source blocks with plain-text comparison response.

nodes.skill_target: distinguish unnamed beloved disciple from external identification
nodes.player_prompt: Яке твердження НЕ слід робити T1 лише з Ів 13:22–25: що учень прямо названий Іваном.
nodes.accepted_answer: The passage does not explicitly name the beloved disciple as John.
nodes.accepted_variants: Equivalent 'not stated in the cited text' wording.
nodes.rejected_answers: The verses explicitly give the personal name John.
nodes.success_feedback: Source-limit preserved: the beloved disciple remains unnamed in John 13:22–25 for this grading task.
nodes.partial_feedback: If you gave an external identification, relabel it as outside the cited text rather than T1.
nodes.failure_feedback: Read the nouns used in John 13:22–25; ask whether a personal name appears in these verses.

hints.H3: The passage says the disciple whom Jesus loved.
hints.H4: Traditional identification is not the same as direct naming here.
hints.H5: 'Not stated in the cited text' is a valid answer.
hints.H7: GUIDED ANSWER: John 13:22–25 does not explicitly name the beloved disciple as John. Any identification belongs outside this T1 claim. Mastery=guided.
